findings.summary: M5.51's new 'the undercount mattered' sentence cites the wrong consequence: the only THREE that exists in the tree INCLUDES `released`, so moving it would have killed M5.28's swap and left M5.31's counter out instead
findings.detail: The row now argues: `M5.28's cited swap involves released, so a fix that moved only three would have left that very swap expressible`. That only follows if the omitted fourth is `released`. The one concrete THREE in the tree is `CommitProtocolSweepTest`'s own comment, corrected in this same commit -- and it named the three components that existed at the `Result` construction before M5.31: `released`, `refusedForAnotherPod`, `refusalsSeen`. Moving those three INCLUDES `released` and therefore does kill the M5.28 swap; what it leaves outside the record is `releasedDespiteOwnPartition`, which is M5.51's own headline transposition. So the conclusion (the undercount mattered) survives, but the reason given is most likely inverted and is in any case unestablished -- the row does not say which three the earlier draft named. Failure scenario: an agent picks up M5.51, reads this sentence as the acceptance criterion ('make sure `released` is inside the record'), moves exactly {released, refusedForAnotherPod, refusalsSeen} into the meter's record, leaves the new `releasedDespiteOwnPartition` as a loose trailing `int`, and marks the row done -- with the exact swap M5.51 was opened for (`refusedForAnotherPod()` where `releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` belongs) still expressible and still suite-green, because both are honestly 0. That is the same class of defect this round's edit was made to remove.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent picks up M5.51, reads this sentence as the acceptance criterion ('make sure `released` is inside the record'), moves exactly {released, refusedForAnotherPod, refusalsSeen} into the meter's record, leaves the new `releasedDespiteOwnPartition` as a loose trailing `int`, and marks the row done -- with the exact swap M5.51 was opened for (`refusedForAnotherPod()` passed where `releasedDespiteOwnPartition()` belongs) still expressible and still suite-green, because both counters are honestly 0 on a correct tree. The sweep silently loses its only view of the wrongly-ALLOWED direction, which is the whole of M5.31.

findings.summary: M5.51's replacement deferral rationale says the record is one 'every protocol test constructs against'; no test constructs a `Result` -- there is exactly one construction site and it is inside `CommitProtocolSimulation` itself
findings.detail: Measured on this tree: `CommitProtocolSimulation.Result` is constructed at exactly one site, `CommitProtocolSimulation.java:621`. Seven test files call `CommitProtocolSimulation.run(...)` / `runForwarding(...)` (FaultClassEvidenceTest, CommitProtocolSweepTest, CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest, CommitProtocolForwardingTest, CommitProtocolSimulationTest, DeferredWriteTest, CommitProtocolForwardingSweepTest) but every one of them only READS accessors, none constructs a Result and none uses a record pattern over it; only `CommitProtocolSweepTest` reads the four release components, which is the row's own measured half and is correct. So the clause left standing as the NEW deferral rationale re-introduces a size over-estimate one sentence after the row deletes the old one ('it is about three files rather than the multi-file change that draft used as its deferral rationale'). Failure scenario: the next agent doing `next-task` sizing reads 'a type change to a record every protocol test constructs against', budgets for touching seven protocol-test files, and defers M5.51 again on a cost that does not exist -- the change is one constructor call site, one reader, and the meter.
findings.failure_scenario: The next agent sizing M5.51 during `next-task` reads 'a type change to a record every protocol test constructs against', budgets for editing seven protocol-test files, and defers the row again on a cost that does not exist -- the real surface is one constructor call site (CommitProtocolSimulation.java:621), one reader (CommitProtocolSweepTest), and the meter. That is the same over-estimate the row deletes one sentence earlier.
